propositions.text: Seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA.

propositions.text: Appeared without counsel at hearing
Requested 30-day adjournment to retain new counsel
Panel inquired about efforts to obtain counsel since July 6, 2010
Spoke to two lawyers who declined to represent him
Considered factors in Rule 48(4) for adjournment request
Claimant had over two years to prepare and over two months to find counsel
Claimant did not demonstrate serious effort to be ready for hearing
Denied adjournment request due to unreasonable delay
Indicated willingness to proceed without counsel if adjournment denied
Confirmed claimant was ready to proceed after denial

paragraphs.summary: The applicant appeared without counsel, requested a 30-day adjournment which the panel denied for lack of serious effort and unreasonable delay; applicant proceeded unrepresented.

propositions.text: Granted asylum in USA in 2000 as Rwandan national
Obtained US permanent resident status in 2005 on same basis
US DHS served notice to cancel asylum status due to belief claimant is Ugandan national
Received notice to appear for US deportation hearing
Visited Canada after hearing nothing from US authorities
Learned asylum status cancelled after failing to appear
Sought refugee protection in Canada
Alleges previous Rwandan nationality declarations were misrepresentations
Alleges detention in Uganda in 1999 due to acquaintance with opponent of government
Entered USA in 1999 on non-immigrant visa and applied for asylum in 2000

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges misrepresented Rwandan nationality, was detained in Uganda, and sought asylum in USA before seeking protection in Canada.

propositions.text: Minister served notice of intention to intervene by documents
Intervention related to claimant's credibility assessment based on US DHS information

paragraphs.summary: The respondent intervened regarding claimant's credibility based on US DHS information.

propositions.text: Minister's intervention did not address exclusion issue
Exclusion issue included in hearing screening form dated April 22, 2010
Claimant had adequate notice that exclusion issue would be raised

paragraphs.summary: Although the Minister did not address exclusion, the claimant had adequate notice it would be raised at hearing.

propositions.text: Determines claimant has US permanent resident status and is excluded from refugee protection
Alternatively, claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection
Determinative issues were claimant's identity and credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant excluded due to US permanent resident status or alternatively not a refugee or protected person, focusing on identity and credibility.

propositions.text: Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions.

propositions.text: Article 1E of UN Refugee Convention excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights in country of residence

paragraphs.summary: Article 1E of the UN Refugee Convention excludes persons recognized as nationals by their country of residence.

propositions.text: Immigration Officer seized US Refugee Travel Document and US permanent resident card
Claimant testified documents are genuine and presented at Pearson Airport in 2008

paragraphs.summary: Documents seized include US permanent resident card and travel document, which claimant testified were genuine and presented at entry.

propositions.text: Permanent resident status in USA triggers Article 1E exclusion
Permanent resident card creates rebuttable presumption of status
Claimant's asylum was terminated in 2008 but permanent resident status not addressed
Claimant felt he lost permanent resident status in 2008
Panel disagrees; claimant remains permanent resident until deportation order issued
Claimant introduced notice to appear for deportation hearing in 2008
Claimant chose not to appear fearing removal
US DHS states claimant failed to appear for termination interview and asylum terminated; no info on further action

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's permanent resident status continues despite asylum termination; claimant failed to appear for deportation hearing fearing removal.

propositions.text: US DHS disclosure confirms claimant subject to deportation hearing
No record of deportation order issued against claimant
Claimant has no evidence of deportation order

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence of a deportation order against claimant and accepts claimant's lack of such evidence.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, claimant remains US permanent resident and is excluded under Article 1E and s. 98 IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant remains US permanent resident and is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E and s. 98 IRPA.

propositions.text: Claimant declined to affirm contents of Personal Information Form (PIF) at hearing
Claimant admitted signature on PIF and understood it was equivalent to oath

paragraphs.summary: The claimant declined to affirm the PIF but admitted signing it and understood it was under oath.

propositions.text: PIF contained multiple untruthful items including birthplace, nationality, family, education, arrest, residence, passport, and narrative
Claimant said he assumed Rwandan identity to improve asylum chances in USA
Claimant maintained false identity through US permanent residence and refugee travel document
Claimant resolved to be truthful in Canada but maintained false identity in application and PIF
Claimant's change of heart came only after Minister's disclosure in June 2010

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant misrepresented identity extensively, maintained false identity in US and Canada, and changed only after Minister's disclosure.

propositions.text: Claimant has no evidence to corroborate Ugandan identity or persecution
Only evidence on core issues is claimant's uncorroborated testimony
Claimant demonstrated willingness to misrepresent identity over eleven years
Panel gives little weight to claimant's testimony about identity and events in Uganda

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's uncorroborated testimony unreliable due to long-term misrepresentations and gives it little weight.

propositions.text: Yip decision requires claimant to establish identity on balance of probabilities
Kante decision requires claimant to bring all evidence believed necessary to prove claim
Claimant introduced no evidence to prove identity or Ugandan nationality
Rule 7 requires claimant to document identity and claim elements
Claimant has not discharged burden of proof on identity; true identity unknown

paragraphs.summary: The court applies precedent requiring proof of identity, finds claimant failed to prove Ugandan identity, and does not know claimant's true identity.

propositions.text: S. 106 IRPA requires considering documentation and explanations regarding identity for credibility
Claimant has not satisfied statutory obligation on documentation and credibility
Draws negative inference on claimant's credibility
Without knowing true identity, claimant not a Convention refugee

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to meet documentation obligations, negatively infers credibility, and concludes claimant is not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Insufficient reliable evidence claimant faces danger of torture or risk to life or cruel treatment
Claimant is not a person in need of protection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no sufficient evidence of risk of torture or cruel treatment and concludes claimant is not in need of protection.

propositions.text: Determines claimant excluded from refugee protection under s. 98 IRPA
Alternatively, claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection and claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court excludes claimant from refugee protection under s. 98 IRPA and alternatively rejects claim as not refugee or protected person.
